subject: Annual commitment options and ramp scenarios for FastFin
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ortiz <elena.ortiz@fastfin.com>, FastFin Procurement <procurement@fastfin.com>
Cc: 
Date: 2026-10-12T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Annual commit options for FastFin — starter/growth/enterprise overview

Hi Elena / FastFin procurement team,

Following our conversation last week, attached is a concise set of annual-commit options tailored to FastFin's roadmap and burst profile. High-level summary below — full models attached (FastFin_commit_vs_usage_model_v1.xlsx):

- Starter: 50M tokens/year — for proof-of-concept and light internal tooling. Effective per-token: $0.00085 with 8% off list (monthly true-up).
- Growth: 250M tokens/year — for broader product rollouts. Effective per-token: $0.00065 with 22% off list (quarterly reporting + 10% buffer).
- Enterprise: 1B tokens/year — production scale with priority capacity. Effective per-token: $0.00045 with 40% off list (annual true-up + committed burst buckets).

Key commercial terms we recommend: 12-month commitment window, quarterly usage reporting, overage rate = 110% of committed per-token price (to keep incentives aligned), 45-day net invoice terms for card/bank transfer (or 30 days for annual prepay). We can add a ramp schedule (month-by-month crediting) if helpful.

Questions for you:
- Which commit band best matches your Q1 product rollout?
- Do you need monthly billing or annual prepay for procurement?
- Any legal or SOC-2 evidence you want packaged with the agreement early?

I can put together a short DocuSign-ready term sheet once you confirm band and billing preference.

Thanks,
Ben
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0142

Attachments: FastFin_commit_vs_usage_model_v1.xlsx
From: Elena Ortiz <elena.ortiz@fastfin.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: FastFin Procurement <procurement@fastfin.com>, Marco Ruiz <marco@fastfin.com>
Date: 2026-10-12T11:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Annual commit options for FastFin — starter/growth/enterprise overview

Ben — thanks for the clear options. A few follow-ups from procurement and finance:

1) Ramp: our usage is expected to be low in months 1-3 and then spike in months 6–12 as we onboard internal teams. Can you confirm whether you support monthly ramp credits or will require a flat consumption curve?
2) Overage: 110% of committed price — can that be softened to 105% for Enterprise?
3) Billing: procurement prefers annual invoiced prepay for 10% additional discount if we prepay 12 months. Does Redwood have standard language for prepay discounts?
4) Security: Marco asked for SOC 2 Type II evidence and your data retention policy.

If we can get a documented ramp profile and prepay mechanics, we can fast-track to legal.

—Elena
Elena Ortiz
Head of Procurement, FastFin
elena.ortiz@fastfin.com
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: 2026-10-12T12:05:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: FastFin questions — ramp, prepay, overage concession?

Laura / Karthik — forwarding FastFin's follow-ups. Quick proposal below I think will close:

- Ramp: offer month-by-month ramp credits for the first 6 months. Credits equal to 50% of gap between committed run-rate and actual usage for months 1–3, then 25% for months 4–6 (one-time credit applied to next invoice). This addresses their onboarding headroom.
- Overage: reduce to 105% for Enterprise only (1B commit) if they sign annual prepay. Keep 110% for Growth/Starter.
- Prepay discount: standard is 10% for annual prepay — suggest we keep as-is but require prepay clears before effective date. For monthly billing, keep the committed per-token price.
- Security: attach SOC2 summary and data-retention FAQ (I'll include in the redwood_commit_summary_v2.pdf).

I attached a revised price sheet and a simple concession box in the spreadsheet for you both to sign off. If legal can get a short DocuSign term sheet we can loop procurement.

Can you confirm the wording/approval? I'm okay to offer the Enterprise overage concession if we get prepay + 12-month term.

Thanks,
Ben

Attachments: redwood_commit_summary_v2.pdf, FastFin_commit_vs_usage_model_v1.xlsx
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: 2026-10-12T13:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: FastFin questions — ramp, prepay, overage concession?

Ben — good structure. Approve the following commercial levers:

- Month-by-month ramp credits for months 1–6 as you outlined (credits explicit and non-refundable, applied to invoices).
- Enterprise concession: 105% overage only when 1) they commit to 1B tokens/year, 2) sign 12-month term, and 3) prepay annual invoice (10% prepay discount applies).
- Include a one-time onboarding credit of $12,000 (applied to first invoice) for Professional Services coordination — conditional on a committed onboarding SOW.

Ask legal to prepare a 1-page Exhibit A with the commit math (per-token effective price, overage, ramp credit rules, prepay discount) and DocuSign link. Send to procurement for signature.

—Laura
Laura Bennett
Director, Commercial Ops, Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ortiz <elena.ortiz@fastfin.com>, FastFin Procurement <procurement@fastfin.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-05T15:22:00-08:00
Subject: Updated proposal and DocuSign link — FastFin commit (Starter/Growth/Enterprise)

Elena / Team — per our internal alignment, please find the updated, DocuSign-ready summary and the short Exhibit A (commit math) here: https://app.docusign.com/FF-202611-RedwoodProposal

Snapshot (final proposal):
- Starter: 50M tokens/year — $42,500/year effective (equiv. $0.00085/token). Monthly billing allowed. No prepay discount. Overage = 115% of per-token price.
- Growth: 250M tokens/year — $162,500/year effective (equiv. $0.00065/token). Quarterly true-ups; Overage = 110% of per-token price.
- Enterprise: 1B tokens/year — $450,000/year effective (equiv. $0.00045/token). 10% prepay discount (if paid annually upfront); Overage = 105% (only with prepay). Includes priority capacity and a 2-week migration window for model upgrades.

Ramp credits: months 1–3 = 50% of shortfall applied as invoice credit; months 4–6 = 25% of shortfall. Onboarding credit: $12,000 (applied on first invoice) subject to signed SOW.

Security package: SOC 2 Type II summary and data-retention policy attached in the DocuSign package.

Next steps:
1) Confirm which commit band you want and whether you will prepay.
2) If prepay, we will issue an annual invoice and apply the 10% prepay discount.
3) Sign Exhibit A via DocuSign and we'll route to Legal for the final MSA.

DocuSign link: https://app.docusign.com/FF-202611-RedwoodProposal
HubSpot deal: https://hubspot.example.com/deals/FF-202611

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call if you want to talk numbers.

Ben
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

Ben — thanks. FastFin prefers the Growth band (250M) with annual prepay to lock pricing and to simplify procurement. We will complete the DocuSign today and route payment. Also confirm that onboarding credit will be reflected on the first invoice.

Elena
